key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can learn avalanche dynamics from the Savage-Hutter model, moving from 1D analytical verification to 2D experimental validation with sparse data assistance.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a fast surrogate for predicting granular avalanche runout, depth, and velocity for hazard assessment on slopes and in mountainous terrain.
method: Verified 1D PINNs against analytical solutions for height-only, velocity-only, and coupled conservative formulations.
Extended the framework to 2D cylindrical-pile collapse on an incline and compared against laboratory experiments and TITAN2D.
Added 10 sparse final-deposit points to avoid trivial zero-solution training in the purely physics-based 2D case.
evidence_signal: The coupled 1D model achieved mean RMSEs of 0.043 for height and 0.079 for velocity, while 2D validation reported global height RMSE of 2.7–6.7 mm and wetted-area IoU of 69–81% across four cases.
watch_item: Pure physics-only training in 2D collapsed to the trivial zero solution, so practical deployment depends on sparse observational data and careful loss balancing.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth-Averaged Avalanche Dynamics
